status: Linux 7.3.4 with 50 local Liuqin adaptations shared by Fedora and Recovery. CPU capacities and dynamic power coefficients use the OEM Cape descriptors; Liuqin CPU/LLCC BWMON nodes use mainline bindings with OEM bandwidth tables (Fedora temporary-boot verified on one Tianma unit: three CPU energy domains, PSCI idle accounting, both BWMON bindings and dynamic ICC votes; Recovery validation remains separate). Desktop boot arguments enable guarded 60/90/120/144 Hz switching for Tianma and CSOT; only Tianma has hardware evidence. Backlight probe uses default brightness and panel first-frame sequencing remains enabled. Exact image hardware validation is recorded separately. M81 fuel-gauge refresh follows the OEM periodic property-86 read, with frozen work during sleep and immediate refresh on resume. M81 charger property IDs and deferred vendor change events follow the shipping OEM module. Liuqin reads attached-source PDOs despite the missing UCSI capability flag; authentication uses their USB communication capability. UCSI decodes PPS request voltage/current and selected APDO limits, retaining M81 negotiated-power notifications for fresh RDO values. UCSI refreshes changed partner source capabilities without replacing the partner PD object, with bounded retries after transient registration failures. UCSI records registration only after a successful version read and clears freed connectors across firmware-service recovery. PMIC GLINK notification subscription and synchronous UCSI registration retry transient failures with bounded per-service budgets. Recovery rejects stale service results, drains work before client release, and resets asynchronous initialization state while cleaning partial ports before retry. UCSI GLINK validates complete read and write response lengths before accessing reply data. Liuqin USB-C DisplayPort keeps the OEM HBR2 ceiling and limits the lane count to the sink and the negotiated Type-C mux assignment. The MSM DP driver acknowledges a standalone PLL unlock during AUX idle without logging an AUX error. Liuqin connects the AudioReach DISPLAY_PORT_RX_0 backend to the MSM DP0 audio codec. MSM DP synchronously closes DPCM playback backends before link teardown and restores still-open frontends after the first DPU frame, independently of physical jack state. ALSA preparation and clocked audio MMIO are serialized; runtime route errors remain visible. Link-managed playback defers HDMI engine shutdown to component close, after CPU DAI shutdown has stopped its DSP graph; legacy/capture timing is unchanged. Four analog microphones use the OEM bias wiring, separate SoundWire master ports with OEM lanes/offsets and four-channel codec-DMA capture. TX mixer counts and mute cover all active decimators. Explicitly blocked display routes remain probeable without starting their backends; missing routes still fail. Four-channel Liuqin capture uses consecutive DSP channel identities to retain every physical microphone. WCD938x follows OEM TX-only codec IRQ ownership; status draining validates resources, read errors and bounded progress. Qualcomm SoundWire disables and drains its IRQ before gating the bus clock and reenables it after successful clock restoration. SoundWire v1.7 pairs the EE1 link manager with CPU1 FIFO registers and completion/error IRQ bits. WCD IRQ ownership, stop/start exclusion and v1.7 CPU1 FIFO changes were temporary-boot verified on one Liuqin unit: clean startup and eight runtime-PM cycles, repeated four-channel capture, software mute/volume and concurrent protected-speaker playback/capture. M81 retains the last valid battery readings only during transient transport loss and reports charging status as unknown, without hiding genuine zero or initial failures. Liuqin stops DSP graphs and SoundWire data ports before DAPM powers down during system suspend, and resets the playback queue during ALSA reprepare. ADSP service recovery preserves the PRM clock provider, rejects offline transport requests, restores votes and ordered device PM state, resets LPASS pins and SoundWire enumeration, and reinitializes WCD and microphone mixer state. Temporary-boot hardware checks on one Liuqin unit verify protected-speaker and four-channel capture recovery across s2idle, a controlled whole-ADSP restart, and s2idle after that restart, including actual audio and data progress. The diagnostic build enables PM_DEBUG and PM_SLEEP_DEBUG; runtime diagnostic output was disabled for the combined recovery checks. Transient errors during forced transport loss remain visible. Earlier kernels occasionally showed a GPIO46 wake interrupting sleep after boot or repeated recovery; its root cause was not confirmed; deep sleep, long-duration operation, external DP audio across sleep/restart, arbitrary firmware crashes and Recovery validation remain separate. Liuqin retains shared WCD ADC clocks until the final active input closes, uses OEM sample-rate-dependent analog HPF gate delays, and drains delayed unmute/filter work before shutdown or card removal. Offline capture teardown retires cached ADC/MICBIAS votes without accessing the volatile SoundWire bank-rate register. The fixed four-slot capture carrier keeps inactive slots clocked and muted while another input remains active. Temporary-boot checks verify single-input startup, partial ADC removal/restoration, rapid capture cycles, four-channel s2idle and controlled ADSP recovery, followed by release of capture clocks and bias enables. Liuqin retires STOP/CLOSE graph commands locally only when the owning GPR service is confirmed offline, including transport reset during a wait; host references and ports still close, and online failures remain visible. DPU physical cleanup clears stale software flush masks before assembling the current teardown, following the reviewed upstream fix; hardware reset, teardown updates and commit timeout checks remain enabled. Temporary-boot checks on one Tianma unit verify four-channel capture recovery through repeated controlled ADSP restarts and actual s2idle, plus 120 Hz display sleep/DPMS restoration with advancing frame counters and clear CTL/DSC flush registers. No APM STOP -102 or DPU commit timeout recurred in these short tests; arbitrary firmware crashes and long-duration display recovery remain separate. Nanosic handles GPIO46 status edges continuously while awake, following the OEM IRQ registration. The driver replaces the I2C dedicated wake handler with a managed ordinary wake IRQ, retaining system wake policy and data IRQ wakeup. Status IRQs perform no I2C or synthetic input; both suspend-time handlers honor disabled wake policy. Temporary-boot checks on one Liuqin unit confirm that GPIO46 is enabled and handles status edges while awake. First, rapid and post-key s2idle tests reach RTC wake; a Shift key wakes through the data IRQ, while disabled keyboard wake holds sleep until RTC. Driver unbind/rebind releases and reacquires both IRQs, followed by a verified Shift press/release and another RTC sleep. No early GPIO46 wake or IRQ ownership warning occurred in these checks; the prior intermittent cause and long-duration behavior remain unconfirmed. Installed-default normal-boot checks on the same unit confirm the matched module/topology set, four-channel desktop capture data, speaker calibration and silent playback progress, continuously enabled GPIO46 and RTC s2idle recovery. The project updater confirmed the new boot and restored disabled automatic writes; external DP audio was not retested during this default update. SM8475 uses the fixed OEM 13-point 220-900 MHz GPU table, GX and independent CX RPMh corners and ACD controls. A730 converts complete optional CX dependencies through cmd-db into GEN7 HFI entries; missing tables retain the legacy disabled value. GMU 200/500 MHz OPPs and the existing A730 bandwidth table already match the OEM. Temporary and installed-default normal boots on one Liuqin unit verify all 13 OPPs in both directions, a three-minute 900 MHz GLES load, automatic DVFS/runtime suspend, GLES render/compute readback, Turnip Vulkan, Rusticl GPU computation and four RTC s2idle recoveries. No GMU/IOMMU error occurred in these bounded checks. Analog voltage readback, thermal limiting, long-duration load, arbitrary GPU fault recovery, full OpenCL CTS and Recovery hardware validation remain separate. A730 preserves SP/TPL1 non-context bank modes in the IFPC/preemption restore list, matching OEM GEN7 behavior. Targeted image and rectangular-copy CTS, plus GLES render/compute readback, are verified on one unit; asynchronous strided-copy correctness requires the documented Fedora Mesa noearlypreamble workaround, and complete OpenCL conformance remains unverified. Liuqin A730 uses a bounded 5000 ms hangcheck interval for long desktop compute dispatches; hardware fault handling and progress retries remain enabled. Temporary and installed-default normal boots on one unit verify the default interval, long compute readback and subsequent GLES/OpenCL operation. A controlled non-progressing compute task verifies bounded hang detection and recovery. Full OpenCL conformance and Recovery hardware validation remain separate.
